title: Percentage of Primary 1 Students Who Had Not Completed Preschool Education
what_it_is: Percentage of Primary 1 Students Who Had Not Completed Preschool Education

sections.label: Preschool enrolment and tracking data
sections.summary: About nine in 10 Singaporean children who entered Primary 1 in 2019 had at least three years of preschool, and outcomes of children who did not attend preschool are not tracked.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: For the cohort of Singaporean children who entered Primary 1 in 2019, about nine in 10 were enrolled in preschools from age four onwards and would have had at least three years in preschool.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: At least 99% would have had some preschool experience before starting Primary 1.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If there were studies made, would the Minister of State be able to share with us the data, and if there were no studies, would one be conducted in the future?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We currently do not track the outcomes of children who did not attend preschool and into Primary school and beyond.

sections.label: Preschool outreach and KidSTART support
sections.summary: ECDA's Preschool Outreach Programme reaches families of children aged three and above not attending preschool, KidSTART is being expanded, and Primary 1 children are screened in the first term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For instance, via ECDA's Preschool Outreach Programme, we work actively with the community to reach out to families of Singaporean children aged three years and above who are not attending preschool.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This can also take the form of helping them with registration forms and seeing what other impediments they may face.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We are also expanding the KidSTART programme, which specifically supports children in the areas that the Member mentioned – health, nutritional needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: One other thing that I wanted to mention is that we also have another gateway at Primary 1 are screened in the first term to see if they need additional help through the Learning Support Programme or Learning Support for Mathematics.

sections.label: Accessible preschool instead of compulsion
sections.summary: Rather than compulsory preschool education, the aim is accessible, affordable and quality preschool, and the Ministry will look at the Member's suggestion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Some of them may feel that there is some advantage in some forms of home-schooling, for instance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, rather than a broad policy of compulsory education in the preschool years, what we have strived to do is to ensure that there is accessible, affordable and quality preschool, so that for any family who has a child and wants to put the child through preschool, there are options available for them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the second question from the Member, the Ministry will take a look at the suggestion that she made.
